name: Drive log coverage from the asset inventory and set retention to the period
description: Make the asset inventory the denominator for log source coverage, alert on sources that stop forwarding, and extend retention to at least the examination period.

steps.action: Reconcile active log sources against the authoritative asset inventory and list the gaps.
Onboard missing sources across identity, infrastructure, application, and endpoint domains.
Alert when a source stops forwarding, so silent dropout is detected rather than discovered.
Set retention to at least the examination period plus a margin, checking platform defaults explicitly.
Record the source list and retention commitment in the logging policy.
Capture dated coverage snapshots so degradation across the period is visible.

implementation_considerations: Retention cost scales with volume and is usually the real constraint; tiering older data to cheaper storage preserves evidenceability without full-price retention.
If the asset inventory is incomplete, that becomes the project. Expect it.
Silent source dropout is more common than never onboarding, and only last-received alerting catches it.
typical_duration: Weeks to onboard sources; retention change is immediate but only accrues coverage forward.

verification_method.how: Reconcile the log source list against the asset inventory for the same date and confirm every in-scope source is forwarding, with configured retention at least as long as the examination period.

residual_risk_note: Coverage assures telemetry exists, not that detection rules would surface anything meaningful from it.
period_limitation_note: Extending retention now cannot recover logs already aged out. An interval already lost stays lost, and this addresses future periods only.
notes: No retention period is prescribed by SOC 2. The examination period is the benchmark DriftGuard applies.
